answer: Distributed Graph Congestion Pricing. Agents pay an access fee scaled inversely to the local edge density of their cluster. To hide inside a dense, synthetic umber cluster of sybils, an attacker must pay a routing toll that multiplies exponentially with node degree. Crossing the structural canyon between isolated clusters requires heavy bandwidth deposits. The ledge of profitability drops below zero once the attacker spawns enough peers to saturate local network capacity, pricing out mass replication through self-inflicted congestion.
